solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Process that removes fine bits from Lord of the Rings, possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters could be a different thing if rearranged, so they are reshuffled

blocks.note: the title of Tolkien's novel, all fourteen letters used

explanation.surface: Someone sees editing that strips small details out of Tolkien's epic as a kind of process.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of the novel's title rearrange to LONGSHORE DRIFT; 'fine bits' are grains of sand and shingle, not details of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Longshore drift is the coastal process in which waves carry sand and shingle along a beach, so it carries off fine particles.

clue.text: Seafood restaurant in new bay resort

indicators.note: something new has been made over, so the letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A fish restaurant has opened in a freshly built seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the resort, but it signals that the letters of 'bay resort' are to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bar is an eatery specialising in shellfish such as oysters, served at a counter.

clue.text: Good mass transit option is something highly sought-after

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
trains are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A commuter praises a good public transport choice as something everyone wants.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single compliment, but 'Good' is just G and the transport option is RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail was the object of the Arthurian quest, so a grail is any coveted goal people chase.

clue.text: Aspire mostly to put the kibosh on kids’ game

indicators.note: 'mostly' means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to aspire is to hope; HOPE without its last letter
to scotch a plan is to put a stop to it

explanation.surface: Someone wants to put an end to a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: HOPE loses its E, then SCOTCH, meaning to quash, follows. 'Put the kibosh on' is an idiom for stopping something; 'on' simply links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground pastime where children hop through numbered squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Right loop for every cowgirl, perhaps

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the letter O is shaped like a loop
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A cowgirl swings exactly the right lasso loop at every attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: The rope imagery fits the definition, but each word stands alone: R, O for its shape, and PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowgirl on a ranch lassoes cattle with a rope, and someone who does that is a roper; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Don’t don smart attire for lecture

blocks.note: first meaning: wear casual clothes rather than formal ones
second meaning: to scold or reprimand someone

explanation.surface: Advice not to wear formal clothes when giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lecture' looks like a university talk to dress for, but it is a verb meaning to tell someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both choosing casual clothing and giving someone a stern telling-off.

clue.text: Club comedy ultimately displaying wry humour

indicators.note: 'ultimately' means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: an iron is a type of golf club
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A comedy club whose acts end up showing a dry, sardonic wit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a comedy venue, but it is a golf club, the IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is a dry style of humour that says the opposite of what is meant, which is what wry wit does.

clue.text: Missile is very loud when losing its tip

indicators.note: a tip is an end point, and losing it means the opening letter goes

blocks.note: strident means harsh and very loud; drop its S

explanation.surface: A missile screams loudly until its nose cone comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: STRIDENT, meaning shrill and loud, loses its first letter. 'tip' here is the front of the word, not of a warhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the name of the submarine-launched nuclear ballistic missile used by the UK and US navies.

clue.text: Doesn’t rise until at the end? That is wrong

indicators.note: 'at the end' points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: last letter of the word
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (Latin id est)
a sin is a moral wrong

explanation.surface: Someone stays in bed till the very end of the morning, and a disapproving voice calls it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends one sentence, but the wordplay runs across it: L, then IE, then SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in is to stay in bed later than usual in the morning, so the sleeper does not get up.

clue.text: Social media app partially reinstalled

indicators.note: 'partially' means only in part, so a section of the following word is used

blocks.note: the run of letters sits inside this word

explanation.surface: A phone user has only managed to reinstall part of a social media app.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'reINSTAlled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insta is the common informal short name for Instagram, the photo-sharing platform.

clue.text: Spicy snacks go with beer from Italy

definitions.note: the answer is a mass noun; the plural definition covers slices of it

blocks.note: go and pep both mean energy or vigour
Peroni is an Italian lager brand

explanation.surface: Hot snacks are best washed down with an Italian beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is a noun here, meaning energy, giving PEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy cured sausage, often eaten sliced as a snack or on pizza.

clue.text: That lady rebuffed demand for varnish

indicators.note: to rebuff is to push back, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: the pronoun for a woman
a call for something is a demand for it

explanation.surface: A woman turned down someone's insistence that she apply varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' reads as refused in the surface, but here it only turns the word for a demand round; the pronoun goes in front unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin secreted by the lac insect, dissolved in alcohol to make a wood finish or lacquer.

clue.text: Take 5 years — primarily lacking enthusiasm — to do a makeover

indicators.note: 'primarily' means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: to take five is to have a short break
Y is the abbreviation for years
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone takes five years, listlessly, to get round to a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take 5' looks like an instruction with a number, but it is the idiom for a short break, REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To restyle is to give something a new look or design, which is what a makeover does.

clue.text: Wealthy individual sobs endlessly after arrest

indicators.note: 'endlessly' means with no ends, so both outside letters go and the centre stays

blocks.note: to nab is to catch or arrest
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rich man weeps without stopping after being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' in the surface means nonstop, but it trims both ends of the word; 'after' then puts the result second.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was originally a Mughal governor and came to mean a man of great wealth, especially one rich from India.

clue.text: Tough European revolutionary killed in a brutal manner

blocks.note: butch means tough and macho
E is the abbreviation for European
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A hard-line European radical was savagely murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough European revolutionary' reads as one person, but it splits into three abbreviations and synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher someone is to slaughter them savagely, like an animal in an abattoir.

clue.text: Permanent marker?

blocks.note: surface reading: an indelible felt-tip pen
setter's reading: a person who makes marks on skin that never wash off

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a stationery item, but read as 'one who marks permanently' it is a person with an ink needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo artist injects ink into skin to leave designs that last for life, a person who marks indelibly.

clue.text: Time to request church group on a mission

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to request something is to ask for it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: It is time to ask a church's missionary group for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church group' looks like one phrase, but 'church' ends the wordplay and 'group' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a unit assembled for a specific operation, such as military or police assignment.

clue.text: Gut feeling this is how teachers make money?

definitions.text: this is how teachers make money?

blocks.note: first meaning: an instinct reached without reasoning

blocks.clueFragment: this is how teachers make money?
blocks.note: second meaning, split into two words: tutors earn their fees through lessons

explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN TUITION, the word says where a teacher's income comes from: tuition is teaching, and the fees paid for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is knowing something instinctively without conscious reasoning, the sense of a hunch.

clue.text: Throws up after first couple of stiff warm-up exercises

indicators.note: a couple is two, so the opening two letters are kept

blocks.note: the opening two letters
to retch is to heave or vomit

explanation.surface: An athlete is sick after starting some stiff warm-up routines.
explanation.walkthrough: The vomiting comes first in the clue, but 'after' places it second in the answer, behind the two letters taken from 'stiff'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretches are limbering movements done before sport to loosen muscles, a typical part of a warm-up.

clue.text: By the sound of it, be really awful and, er, give in

indicators.note: points to how the words are spoken rather than how they are written

blocks.note: slang: to suck is to be very bad
um and er are both hesitation noises

explanation.surface: Someone who is hopeless at something hesitates, then gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCK plus UM, said together, sound like the answer. 'er' is not a filler in the surface; it is the hesitation that gives UM.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to yield or surrender to pressure, temptation or illness.

clue.text: I hear you like music?

blocks.note: first meaning: a reply acknowledging what someone said
second meaning, playful: having notes, as music does

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as asking whether you enjoy music, but 'like' means resembling, and music is made of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a reply, the word acknowledges a remark; read as an adjective it means furnished with musical notes.

clue.text: Duke joining private for meal

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
inner thoughts are private ones

explanation.surface: A duke joins an army private for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like a soldier, but it is the adjective meaning personal, INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main daily meal, usually eaten in the evening.

clue.text: Part of the eye is able to shut freely

indicators.note: 'freely' means without constraint, so the letters move about at will

blocks.note: can means is able to
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eye is said to be able to close without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN is followed by the letters of 'shut' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The canthus is the corner of the eye, where the upper and lower eyelids meet.

clue.text: Set up some centralised online connection points

indicators.note: 'some' takes only a portion of the letters that follow
in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone sets up central online connection points for a network.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'centraliSED ONline' is SEDON, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a network, nodes are the junctions where links meet and data is passed on.

clue.text: It’s like W-H-E-A-T

blocks.note: surface reading: the word written out letter by letter
setter's reading: a grain similar to wheat, and also the past participle for writing out letters

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphens show a word written out letter by letter, and the answer describes that; it is also an ancient wheat-like grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is a cereal closely related to common wheat, and it is also the British past form of the verb for naming letters.

clue.text: Dissension following legal proceeding

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a legal action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Discord breaks out after a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like 'after', but it is the abbreviation F, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Faction can mean internal strife and discord within a group, not only the breakaway group itself.

clue.text: Republican bound by firm belief system

indicators.note: something bound by another is held inside it

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
in US politics red is the colour of the Republicans

explanation.surface: A Republican is tied to a firmly held set of beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective for the belief, but it is a company, CO, which holds RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of the principles a person lives by, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Boxers maybe subject to deterioration

blocks.note: under the rule of something is subject to it
wear is damage from use

explanation.surface: Prizefighters may be prone to physical decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' looks like fighters, but it means boxer shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose men's shorts worn beneath clothes, an example of underclothing.

clue.text: English low-calorie cream

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
lite is the marketing spelling of light, low in calories

explanation.surface: A tub of reduced-fat English cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cream' looks like dairy but means the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best members, the top tier, just as cream rises to the top of milk.

clue.text: Where you might find the on/off switch is irrelevant

definitions.text: Where you might find the on/off switch

blocks.clueFragment: Where you might find the on/off switch
blocks.note: first meaning: next to a wall socket, which in Britain is called a power point
second meaning: not pertinent to the matter in hand

explanation.walkthrough: A British wall socket is a power point, and it usually has its own switch next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something not relevant to the main issue being discussed.
